title: Open Canonical Review Schema
description: One peer review of one scholarly work, in a form shared by journals, conferences and AI reviewers

$schema.description: The URL of the OCRS schema this review follows: the `$id` of a published version (e.g., 'https://valency-oss.github.io/open-canonical-review-schema/v0.9.0/canonical-review.schema.json'). It tells validators and editors which version to check the review against; it is not part of the review

review_id.description: Identifier of this review, unique within the system that produced the OCRS record

created_at.description: When the review was written; for AI reviews, when the run ended

updated_at.description: When the review was last changed

provenance.description: Where this record came from: the source system, its own identifiers, and how it was mapped to OCRS

source_system.description: The system the review was taken from (e.g., 'hotcrp', 'scholarone', 'openreview', 'openaireview', 'deepreview')

source_review_id.description: The review's identifier in the source system

source_url.description: Link to the review in the source system

review_doi.description: DOI registered for the review itself (e.g., a Crossref peer review DOI), without a resolver prefix. Not the DOI of the work under review, which goes in target.identifiers.doi

license.description: The license the review itself is published under, as the source states it (e.g., OpenReview's 'CC BY 4.0', a JATS <license>). Not the license of the work under review

name.description: The license's name or SPDX identifier, as the source gives it (e.g., 'CC BY 4.0', 'CC-BY-4.0')

imported_at.description: When the review was mapped to OCRS

raw_payload.description: The source system's review exactly as received, kept when the mapper is asked to keep it

mapping.description: How the source review was converted to OCRS

mapping_spec_id.description: Identifier of the mapping specification the mapper follows (e.g., 'canonical-review.mapping.v1')

mapper_version.description: Version of the mapper code that produced this record

lossiness_notes.description: What the mapping lost or changed: source fields with no OCRS field, values coerced to allowed values

referees.description: Who wrote the review: one referee, or each member of a panel or of a joint review (e.g., eLife's joint public reviews)

target.description: The work under review: the exact version the reviewer read. Other versions and forms of it go in relations

work_id.description: The work's primary identifier, as '<type>:<value>', where <type> is its key in identifiers (e.g., 'doi:10.7554/eLife.112155.1'). An internal ID also names its field: 'internal_id:<field_name>:<value>' (e.g., 'internal_id:openreview_forum:2dnO3LLiJ1'). It is the identifier that comes first in the resolution priority of identifiers, or 'unknown' if the source names none

title.description: Title of the work, as the review gives it

identifiers.description: Structured identifiers of the reviewed version, with validation and resolution metadata

version.description: Version of the paper/work being reviewed (e.g., v1, v2)

relations.description: Other versions and forms of the reviewed work, each with how it relates to the reviewed version (e.g., the reviewed version is_new_version_of an earlier one, or is_version_of a preprint)

venue.description: Journal, conference or platform the work was submitted to

track.description: Track, section or category within the venue (e.g., 'main', 'datasets and benchmarks')

revision_of.description: Deprecated: use relations with type 'is_new_version_of'. Identifier of the earlier version this work revises

artifacts.description: Identities of the work’s associated materials, stored once and referenced by ID. These records do not assert that an artifact was assessed or checked.

review_context.description: The circumstances of the review: its kind, stage, round, who asked for it and the time it took. The reviewer's expertise is each referee's own (referees[].expertise)

review_type.description: Kind of review: feedback the authors asked for before submission, a referee's first review, review of a revision, response to a rebuttal, meta-review or editor's report, shepherding, review of a replication, a citation review (one of only the work's references, such as whether each exists and says what it is cited for), an author's comment or response, a community comment, an aggregate of several reviews, or an editor's or recommender's recommendation. Whether it came before or after publication goes in stage

stage.description: Whether the review was written before the work was published (pre_publication) or after (post_publication)

requested_by.description: Who asked for the review: an editor, a program committee chair, or a person or service requesting an AI review

time_spent_hours.description: Hours the reviewer spent on the review

metric_schemas.description: Source forms and local metric definitions, keyed by review-local schema ID.

related_reviews.description: Other reviews this one relates to: one it responds to (an author's response to a report, a reply in a discussion), one it replaces, or ones it summarizes (a meta-review)

metrics.description: Scores the reviewer gave, each on its own scale (e.g., soundness 3 of 4, overall 6 of 10)

findings.description: The review's specific points, grouped by kind

weaknesses.description: Problems in the work: errors, gaps, unsupported claims

comments.description: Points the reviewer makes without saying whether they are strengths, weaknesses or questions. Not counted as weaknesses

changes.description: Changes the reviewer asks for, each with a severity that says how serious the problem is; classify the kind of change with tags

narrative.description: The review's own text, as the source gives it, in its parts and in order: the named text fields of a review form, the headed sections of a report, or one undivided text. `opinion` and `findings` are OCRS's structured reading of it

calibration.description: Information for comparing this reviewer's scores with other reviewers'

reviewer_leniency_z.description: How lenient the reviewer is compared with other reviewers, as a z-score (positive means more lenient)

historical_accept_rate.description: Share of works this reviewer has recommended accepting in the past, from 0 to 1

notes.description: How the calibration values were computed

signatures.description: Cryptographic signatures over this review, so readers can check who wrote it and that it was not changed

value.description: The signature, encoded as the scheme expects

checks.description: Systematic checks run on the work, such as reference verification or AI-text detection, including those that found nothing

text_format.description: How to read the review's free text (opinion, findings, narrative). When absent, the format is unknown

markup.description: Markup in the text: none (plain), Markdown or HTML

math.description: How the text writes mathematics: not at all, or as TeX (e.g., '$\tau$')

extensions.description: Data with no OCRS field, kept under one key per source format (e.g., extensions.openaireview)

work_summary.description: The reviewer’s descriptive account of the work, separate from their opinion.

summary.description: Neutral synopsis of what the work does.

claims.description: Extracted propositions with IDs for findings to reference.

allOf.description: The record contains source-stated review content; identities and rubric definitions alone are not review content.

nonBlank.description: Text that has a character other than whitespace. The review content rule counts only such text

hasTitleOrText.description: A point whose title or text is not blank. The review content rule counts only such points

identifierWithLink.description: An identifier value with optional hyperlink for resolution

internalIdentifier.description: System-specific internal identifier with field name context

field_name.description: Name of the identifier field in the source system (e.g., 'DocumentID', 'hotcrp_pid', 'openreview_forum')

value.description: The identifier's value in the source system

hyperlink.description: URL of the work in the source system

workRelation.description: Another version or form of the reviewed work, and how it relates to the reviewed version

type.description: How the reviewed version relates to this one, read as '<reviewed version> <type> <this work>'. Crossref's intra-work relation types (relations.xsd), plus DataCite's IsNewVersionOf and IsPreviousVersionOf, in snake_case

identifiers.description: Identifiers of this version or form

workIdentifiers.description: Optional structured identifiers for the work. They cover Crossref's identifier types (doi, arxiv, pmid, pmcid, handle, ark, isbn, issn, ecli, accession, purl, uri as permalink, uuid, other as internal_id), plus S2CID, OpenAlex and Valency. Resolution priority: DOI > arXiv > S2CID > PubMed ID > PMCID > OpenAlex > Valency > Handle > ARK > ISBN > ECLI > accession > PURL > permalink > UUID > internal_id. ISSN identifies the journal or series, not the work, so it is never the primary identifier

value.description: The DOI, without a resolver prefix
The PMCID, including the PMC prefix

valency_id.description: Valency Hub work ID (e.g., W_6r533gdt), or the ID of one version of the work (e.g., W_6r533gdt_v2)

value.description: The Valency work ID: 'W_' and at least 8 characters from a-z and 2-9, without i, l and o. A version's ID adds '_v' and the version number

handle.description: Handle (e.g., 20.500.12345/abc or 1721.1/12345). DOIs are also handles; give them in doi

value.description: The handle, without a resolver prefix
The ARK, including the 'ark:' label, without a resolver prefix

hyperlink.description: A resolver URL for the ARK (e.g., https://n2t.net/ark:/13030/tf5p30086k)

isbn.description: ISBN of a book or chapter (e.g., 9780262035613)

value.description: The ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, digits only, without hyphens or spaces; an ISBN-10 may end in X

hyperlink.description: URL of a page for the book

issn.description: ISSN of the journal or series the work appears in (e.g., 2050-084X). It identifies the serial, not the work, so give it alongside an identifier of the work

ecli.description: European Case Law Identifier, for a court decision (e.g., ECLI:EU:C:2014:317)

value.description: The ECLI: country, court, year and number

accession.description: Accession number in a data repository, for a dataset or other deposited record (e.g., MN908947 in GenBank)

database.description: The repository that issued the accession number (e.g., 'GenBank', 'PDB', 'ENA')

hyperlink.description: URL of the record in the repository

purl.description: Persistent URL (PURL) for the work (e.g., https://purl.org/...)

value.description: The UUID in its hyphenated form

content_hash.description: Hash of the work's file: a content-addressed identifier, for checking that a file is the work reviewed

aiRefereeReference.description: Lightweight reference to a third-party AI referee system when full provenance is not available

third_party_id.description: Unique identifier from the third-party AI review system (e.g., 'newco-ai-ref-2sd4f6a')

reference_url.description: URL for more information about the AI reviewer

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the AI system

version.description: Version of the AI reviewer (defaults to v1)

opinion.description: The reviewer’s overall sentiment and optional decision; not a summary of the work.

stance.description: Overall sentiment, independent of the recommendation.

decision.description: Optional explicit acceptance or revision recommendation.

metric_refs.description: Optional overall metric IDs selected for this opinion. No reciprocal reference is stored.

supported_by.description: Optional finding IDs supporting the overall opinion or decision, independently of each score’s support.

referee.description: Who wrote the review: a person, an AI system or both

referee_type.description: Whether a person, an AI system or both wrote the review

identity_mode.description: How the reviewer's and authors' identities are disclosed: triple blind (also hidden from the editors), double blind (hidden both ways), single blind (reviewer hidden), open, pseudonymous, or confidential (known only to the editors)

referee_id.description: The reviewer's identifier in the source system, possibly pseudonymous

competing_interests_declared.description: Whether the reviewer declared a competing interest

competing_interests_statement.description: The reviewer's statement of competing interests

human_referee.description: The human reviewer's identity and expertise. Optional: a fully anonymous review can leave it out

ai_referee.description: The AI reviewer's system, run, inputs, outputs and safety

hybrid_workflow.description: How people and AI shared the work, for hybrid reviews

reproducibility.description: What is needed to run the review again and get the same result

humanReferee.description: Human referee identity and expertise information

scopus_id.description: Scopus Author ID (10-12 digits, no leading zero)

valency_id.description: Valency Hub author ID (e.g., A_7zdytxzb): 'A_' and at least 8 characters from a-z and 2-9, without i, l and o. The author's page is https://hub.valency.io/authors/<id>

google_scholar_id.description: Google Scholar profile ID (12 alphanumeric characters)

name.description: Display name of the reviewer (may be redacted)

affiliation_redacted.description: Whether the affiliation was removed to keep the reviewer anonymous

expertise.description: The referee's expertise in the work's subject

self_reported_level.description: How familiar the reviewer says they are with the subject

domain_tags.description: Subject areas the reviewer is expert in

seed.description: Random seed for reproducing the review process, not the reviewed work; used for stages without an explicit stage seed

seeds.description: Explicit seeds for review stages (e.g., retrieval or generation), overriding the whole-review seed for those stages

stage.description: The stage this seed is for (e.g., 'retrieval', 'generation')

determinism.description: Whether running again should give the same review

intended_deterministic.description: Whether the review is meant to come out the same on every run

notes.description: What can still vary between runs, and why

run_replay.description: How to run this review again

run_id.description: Identifier of the run to replay

replay_command.description: Command that runs the review again

config_ref.description: Where the run's configuration is stored

bundle_ref.description: Where the bundle of everything the run needs is stored

bundle_hash.description: Hash of that bundle, to check it is unchanged

environment_snapshot.description: The environment the review ran in

aiReferee.description: AI referee information - either full provenance or lightweight reference

system.description: The AI system: its framework, provider, models, tools and policies

execution.description: The run: when it ran, how long, on what, and at what cost

inputs.description: What the AI system read: materials, retrieval and prompts

outputs.description: What the AI system wrote, and the tokens it used

safety.description: Guardrails and handling of personal data during the run

reference.description: Lightweight reference to a third-party AI system

oneOf.description: Full provenance: the system and the run, optionally with inputs, outputs and safety, and no reference

critic_framework.description: The review software that ran the models (e.g., OpenAIReview)

version.description: Its version: a release, or a short commit

commit.description: Source commit it was built from

build_id.description: Identifier of the build or container image

platform.description: Platform the models were called through (e.g., 'aws-bedrock')

models.description: Models the system used, each with its role

tools.description: Tools the system called, such as search or code execution

policies.description: The review policy the system followed

role.description: What the model did in the review

model_id.description: Model identifier as the provider names it (e.g., 'us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5')

model_version.description: Model version or snapshot date, when the identifier does not include it

parameters.description: Generation settings, such as temperature or maximum tokens

weights_hash.description: Hash of the model weights, for self-hosted models

invocations.description: How many times the tool was called

wall_time_seconds.description: Elapsed time of the run, in seconds

accelerator.description: GPU or other accelerator, if any

notes.description: Anything else about the compute environment

currency.description: Currency of the amounts, as an ISO 4217 code (e.g., 'USD')

line_items.description: The total broken down by kind of cost

estimation_method.description: How the cost was measured or estimated (e.g., 'LLM gateway spend')

logs_ref.description: Where the run's logs are stored

ref.description: Where the material is, or its name

content_hash.description: Hash of the material, to check it is the same file

retrieval.description: Searches the system made beyond the work itself, such as related literature

corpus.description: What it searched (e.g., a literature index)

top_k.description: How many results it took per search

results_ref.description: Where the search results are stored

prompt_ref.description: Where the prompt text is stored

redaction_applied.description: Whether parts of the stored prompt were removed

generated_artifacts.description: Files the run wrote besides this record

token_usage.description: Tokens used across all model calls

guardrails_triggered.description: Whether any safety guardrail stopped or changed model output

guardrails_notes.description: Which guardrails triggered, and what they did

pii_handling.description: How personal data in the inputs was handled

human_contributions.description: What people did in the review, one item per contribution

attribution.description: How much of the review came from AI and how much from people

ai_fraction_estimate.description: Estimated share of the review from AI, from 0 to 1

human_fraction_estimate.description: Estimated share of the review from people, from 0 to 1

diff_ref.description: Where the person's changes to the AI output are stored

metricAssessment.description: One assessment value, referencing its source form and original scale in review_context.

value.description: The score, as given on its scale

uncertainty.description: Reviewer uncertainty on the original score scale.

justification.description: Why the reviewer gave this score

normalized.description: Optional rescaling of the original value, with its method. This does not establish equivalent meaning across rubrics or make a confidence score a probability.

value_0_1.description: The score on a 0 to 1 scale, where 0 is worst and 1 is best

method_version.description: Version of the normalization method when known.

id.description: Review-local observation ID, unique across addressable records.

definition_ref.description: The exact definition needed to interpret this value.

source_value.description: Original source answer, including its original label or representation when needed for faithful conversion.

supported_by.description: Optional strength, weakness, question or comment IDs explaining the score. Checks and raw measurements reach metrics through findings. A bare source score remains valid.

scale.description: The scale a score is on

type.description: Kind of scale: ordered levels, numbers, yes/no, unordered categories or text

step.description: Distance between allowed values (e.g., 1 for whole numbers)

values.description: The values the scale allows, when they are not every step from min to max (e.g., ICLR's overall rating: 1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10)

units.description: Unit of the values, if any

description.description: What the scale measures, as the source system explains it

metricValue.description: A score: a number, yes/no, a label, or a list of them

probability.description: How likely the reviewer thinks a statement holds, from 0 (certainly not) to 1 (certainly)

credence.description: How confident the reviewer is in their probability, from 0 (a guess) to 1 (certain of it). Credence is about the estimate, not the statement: a reviewer can think something very likely (probability 0.9) and hold that view loosely (credence 0.3). Optional, but we strongly encourage it alongside probability, which it needs: it helps readers tell a firm judgement from a tentative one

check.description: A reported human, AI or tool examination. Do not invent an examination from a reviewer assertion.

kind.description: Check kind, such as reference_verification, statistics, availability or artifact_execution; custom namespaced kinds are allowed.

performed_by.description: The tool or service that ran the check. When absent, the referee ran it

name.description: Name of the tool or service (e.g., 'Pangram')

referee_id.description: Identifier of the human or AI referee performing the check.

outcome.description: The check's verdict, as the source states it: no issues, issues found, inconclusive, or not run. Leave out when the source gives only results

summary.description: The result, as the source wrote it

procedure.description: Reported examination method and optional script artifact reference.

artifact_id.description: ID of a procedure or script in target.artifacts.

execution_status.description: Execution status, separate from the content’s correctness.

run_ref.description: Reference to logs or detailed run provenance.

results_coverage.description: What the result list covers; absence does not mean every item was checked.

results.description: Individual observations, with evidence stored here rather than repeated on the check.

suggestedEdit.description: A rewrite the reviewer proposes for a passage of the work

original.description: The exact text to replace, when the reviewer states it. When absent, the reviewer gave only the new text, and the point's evidence links show the passage it concerns

replacement.description: The text the reviewer proposes instead

section.description: One part of the review's own text: a named field of a review form, a headed section of a report, or the whole text

title.description: The part's heading, or the name of the form field it fills, as the source gives it

role.description: What the part is, when the source says: the reviewer's summary, the main text of the review, the questions for the authors, or something else

audience.description: Who the source shows the part to: everyone, the authors, the other reviewers, or the editors or committee only. When absent, the source does not say

reviewRelation.description: Another review this one relates to, and how

type.description: How this review relates to the other: it responds to it, it replaces it, or it summarizes it

review_id.description: The other review's review_id, or its identifier in the source system

doi.description: The other review's DOI, without a resolver prefix

evidenceLink.description: One plain source pointer, embedded where needed; interpretation belongs in the finding, not a support/contradiction flag.

version.description: Source document version, artifact commit or dataset revision.

location.description: Optional named or positional source location.

quote.description: Optional exact source excerpt; if a span is supplied, it equals the selected slice.

evidenceLocation.description: Optional named locations and ranges, combinable with a positional span; page and section never change a span’s origin.

page.description: One-based page number in the referenced document

page_end.description: Last page, for a passage spanning several pages; at least page

label.description: Location in the source’s own words, including named pages or Roman page labels.

prefix.description: Text immediately before quote, to disambiguate repeated passages.

suffix.description: Text immediately after quote, to disambiguate repeated passages.

line_start.description: One-based inclusive first line in the referenced source.

line_end.description: One-based inclusive last line in the referenced source.

span.description: Exact positional span in a fixed text representation.

text_anchor.description: Exact text with optional immediately surrounding text to distinguish repeated passages

exact.description: Exact sentence or passage being referenced

prefix.description: Text immediately before the exact passage

suffix.description: Text immediately after the exact passage

writtenReport.description: Optional written report document submitted alongside the structured review

filename.description: Original filename of the uploaded report

content_type.description: Format of the written report (PDF, Word document, Markdown, or plain text)

url.description: URL or reference to the uploaded file

uploaded_at.description: Timestamp when the report was uploaded

description.description: Optional description of the report contents

definitionRef.description: An exact metric definition in this review’s context. JSON Schema cannot check that it resolves; ocrs.validate_canonical does, and other validators must check it themselves.

metricSource.description: Source form identity and original rubric, as supplied; omit unknown metadata.

review_type.description: Kind of review this form is for.

catalog_ref.description: Catalog used to interpret canonical metric keys.

snapshot.description: Original source form or rubric, unchanged.

metricDefinition.description: One source field’s meaning and original scale. Identity remains distinct from its canonical dimension.

label.description: Metric name as the source displays it.

dimension.description: Canonical metric dimension from the closed vocabulary. review_confidence expresses confidence in the overall review; confidence remains valid for existing source mappings. Use other for an unlisted source criterion and retain its original label and prompt.

scale.description: Original scale, with all supplied bounds, values, point labels and units.

direction.description: How to interpret direction; confidence and raw quantities do not automatically measure merit.

metricSchema.description: One external or locally authored review form, stored once.

definitions.description: Metric definitions keyed by source field identity.

artifact.description: Identity of an associated material. Store evaluations in findings and observed test results in checks.

id.description: Review-local artifact ID, unique across all addressable records. JSON Schema cannot check uniqueness across records; ocrs.validate_canonical does.

ref.description: URL, repository, DOI or source-described location, when known. Do not invent a location for absent or inaccessible material.

version.description: Exact revision, commit or release, when known.

content_hash.description: Hash identifying the exact artifact contents.

reported_availability.description: Availability as the source states it, in the 0.8 vocabulary. An actual access test is a check result; omission is not a claim of availability.

decision.description: The reviewer's recommendation to the editor or committee

recommendation.description: Recommended acceptance outcome, independent of any required revision

revision_requirement.description: Revision required independently of the acceptance recommendation: none, minor, major, or unspecified when revision is requested without its extent. Omit when unknown or not provided

source_label.description: The recommendation in the source's own words, verbatim, when the source gives it in words (e.g., 'Accept (Oral)', F1000's 'Approved with Reservations'). A recommendation given as a score keeps its label on that score's metric instead. `recommendation` and `revision_requirement` are OCRS's reading of it

rationale.description: Why the reviewer recommends this, in brief

uncertainty.description: Reviewer uncertainty, not extraction confidence. Findings use probability; metric scores may use interval. Never use both.

probability.description: Probability that this finding’s assertion holds.

credence.description: Confidence in assigning this probability or metric estimate.

interval.description: Plausible interval on the original metric scale.

rationale.description: Source explanation, including qualitative uncertainty without an invented number.

findingUncertainty.description: Shared uncertainty on a finding: probability, optional associated credence and rationale; no interval.

metricUncertainty.description: Shared uncertainty on a metric: interval, credence and rationale; no finding probability.

contentRef.description: A typed reference to derived material within this review.

id.description: An existing review-local ID of the indicated type.

finding.description: One source-stated strength, weakness, question or comment. Do not create a point solely to justify a rating.

id.description: Identifier of this point, unique among all the review's addressable records (findings, claims, contributions, artifacts, checks, check results and metrics), so that other records can refer to it

text.description: The point in full, as the reviewer wrote it

title.description: Short headline for the point, as the reviewer wrote it

group.description: Headings the point appears under in the review, outermost first, as the reviewer wrote them (e.g., ['Methods', 'Minor comments'])

evidence_links.description: Places in the work the point refers to

about.description: Optional claims, contributions, checks or check results interpreted by this finding; prefer result IDs for individual outcomes.

uncertainty.description: Probability of this assertion, optional associated credence and rationale.

weakness.description: One problem or limitation, with optional seriousness independent of its probability.

id.description: Identifier of this point, unique among all the review's addressable records (findings, claims, contributions, artifacts, checks, check results and metrics), so that other records can refer to it

text.description: The point in full, as the reviewer wrote it

title.description: Short headline for the point, as the reviewer wrote it

group.description: Headings the point appears under in the review, outermost first, as the reviewer wrote them (e.g., ['Methods', 'Minor comments'])

evidence_links.description: Places in the work the point refers to

about.description: Optional claims, contributions, checks or check results interpreted by this finding; prefer result IDs for individual outcomes.

uncertainty.description: Probability of this assertion, optional associated credence and rationale.

severity.description: How serious the point is: critical, it invalidates the work's main conclusions, such as a fatal flaw in the method or results that do not hold; major, it substantially weakens the conclusions or how well they are supported, such as a missing analysis or an unjustified claim; minor, it does not affect the main conclusions, such as a missing reference or a small error that leaves the results unchanged; trivial, it is cosmetic, such as typos, clarity issues, formatting or wording; info, it reports no problem, such as a remark

change.description: One requested action. Keep OR alternatives in one item when any one is sufficient; split independently requested actions.

id.description: Identifier of this point, unique among all the review's addressable records (findings, claims, contributions, artifacts, checks, check results and metrics), so that other records can refer to it

text.description: The point in full, as the reviewer wrote it

title.description: Short headline for the point, as the reviewer wrote it

severity.description: How serious the point is: critical, it invalidates the work's main conclusions, such as a fatal flaw in the method or results that do not hold; major, it substantially weakens the conclusions or how well they are supported, such as a missing analysis or an unjustified claim; minor, it does not affect the main conclusions, such as a missing reference or a small error that leaves the results unchanged; trivial, it is cosmetic, such as typos, clarity issues, formatting or wording; info, it reports no problem, such as a remark

group.description: Headings the point appears under in the review, outermost first, as the reviewer wrote them (e.g., ['Methods', 'Minor comments'])

suggested_edits.description: Rewrites the reviewer proposes for the work's text. Alternatives for the same text are separate items

evidence_links.description: Places in the work the point refers to

addresses.description: Optional IDs of strengths, weaknesses, questions or comments this change addresses. No inverse list is stored.

contribution.description: A descriptive contribution, not an evaluative strength.

id.description: Identifier of this point, unique among all the review's addressable records (findings, claims, contributions, artifacts, checks, check results and metrics), so that other records can refer to it

text.description: The point in full, as the reviewer wrote it

title.description: Short headline for the point, as the reviewer wrote it

evidence_links.description: Places in the work the point refers to

claim.description: A proposition attributed to the work. Extraction does not endorse its truth.

text.description: The proposition attributed to the work.

representation.description: Whether the claim is quoted or paraphrased.

evidence_links.description: Places in the work the point refers to

checkResult.description: One raw observation. A result need not produce an evaluative finding.

status.description: Result in the source’s own words.

data.description: Raw source measurements or outputs, with units and original structure. These are separate from assessment metrics.

evidence_links.description: Source materials or recorded outputs associated with this result.

resourceRef.description: The referenced source material. Work and review refer to this record; artifact IDs resolve in target.artifacts.

id.description: Artifact ID, required when type is artifact.

work.description: The work the place refers to when it is another work, such as a citation the reviewer says is missing

authors.description: Authors, as the reviewer names them

citation.description: The reference as printed, copied verbatim (e.g., an entry in the work's bibliography)

textSpan.description: A zero-based Unicode code-point range [start, end) in one exact stored text representation. Whitespace and line breaks count without normalization. Offsets are not bytes, tokens or UTF-16 code units.

text_ref.description: Resolvable URI or source ID pinning the exact text version or content hash. Count from the beginning of this entire text, never from a page or section.

end.description: Index immediately after the last included code point; greater than start and no greater than text length.
